newsitem.title: USA: Home Depot confirms dropping Dutch Boy paint.
newsitem.headline: Home Depot confirms dropping Dutch Boy paint.

text.p: Atlanta-based Home Depot Inc confirmed Tuesday that it will drop Sherwin-Williams Co's Dutch Boy paint line and increase its offerings of Imperial Chemical Industries Plc's Glidden brand.
It had carried both brands, with Dutch Boy prevalent in the Northeast and Glidden elsewhere, Kim Shreckengost, Home Depot's director of investor relations, said in a telephone interview.
The home center chain, which has 504 stores in 38 states, will continue to carry Sherwin-Williams' Ralph Lauren paint line, as well as another manufacturer's brand, she said.

Cleveland-based Sherwin-Williams' stock closed at 55 on the New York Stock Exchange Tuesday, recovering $3 of the $4 it lost on Monday when the market learned of the business it lost. Home Depot closed up 7/8 at 51-1/4 on the same exchange.
Shreckengost said the decision was part of an on-going strategic review of assortments in all product categories.
"Going forward, we are about one-third of the way through the process," she said.

Asked if suppliers of other products might be pruned to simplify inventories and ordering, she said, "This is an attempt to continue doing what we do best at Home Depot -- provide the best value to customers at the lowest prices."
Shreckengost added, "It does not necessarily mean we would delete other vendors unless it made sense to do so."
She declined to discuss prices or account value.
Cleveland-based Glidden Co could not immediately be reached for comment.

Sherwin-Williams spokeswoman Lydia Bazarko said the business her company will lose also includes private-label paints Cleveland-based Sherwin-Williams made for Home Depot. Bazarko said that on an annualized basis for Sherwin-Williams in 1997, the lost business will amount to about $60 million.

Bazarko said analysts expect Sherwin-Williams' overall 1997 sales to be about $4.7 billion after it completes its previously announced $830 million acquisition of Thompson Minwax Holding Corp, expected to close shortly.

The lost business amounts to about one percent of Sherwin-Williams' overall sales, said analyst Justin Maurer, who follows Sherwin-Williams for McDonald & Co in Cleveland. He said he expects that to be easily offset.
